name: ml-validate-vs-additive-fields
description: Reference ml 0.10.7: 'ml validate' flags additive/unknown record fields as schema errors ('must NOT have additional properties') even on its own records, but mutating commands (record/outcome/archive/restore) accept and preserve them. ADR-0023 round-trip gates must assert additive-field survival through mutators, never through validate-clean.

name: cli-parity-envelope-channel-contract
description: ml 0.10.7 channel contract (pinned by probe + differential battery): success envelopes and validate/doctor failure envelopes on STDOUT, status-style handled errors on STDERR; JSON pretty 2-space; no-args prints help to stderr exit 1; unknown command = 2-line stderr hint; warnings never fail doctor exit; doctor --fix exits with PRE-fix result; --quiet suppresses init and the doctor plain report but NOT status or the validate summary; --timing prints Bun-style Done in Nms only for parsed CLIs.

name: oneof-schema-empirical-rule
description: Reference oneOf sub-errors: each branch reports its first MISSING required property; a branch with all required present but type-const mismatch reports its FIRST required property (pseudo-missing). Records with unregistered type fail as `Unknown record \`X\`` instead of the oneOf blob. Join is ";  " (semicolon+2 spaces); validate message = "Schema validation failed:  <joined>" (2 spaces after colon); doctor detail = "domain:line -  <joined>" (no wrapper); plain validate prints the wrapper once then 3-space-indented sub lines. Line addressing is PHYSICAL 1-based (blank lines counted).

name: record-family-parity-contract
description: record: auto-create precedes validation AND dry-run (side effects persist); duplicate = exit 0 advisory (record #N, quiet-gated), --force appends same id new recorded_at; ids = mx-+sha256(type:idKeyField)[:6] independent of store/domain/timestamps; flag-path field order: type, classification, recorded_at, evidence?, tags?, relates_to?, supersedes?, dir_anchors?, outcomes?, payload, files?, id (stdin/batch preserves INPUT order, appends recorded_at/classification/id); evidence auto-fills FULL git HEAD sha in git dirs; edit replaces lists, appends absent keys at line end (relates_to, supersedes, files), never recomputes ids, no-op succeeds; outcome objects: record-time {status,duration,test_results,agent} before payload, ml outcome {status,recorded_at,duration,agent,notes,test_results} after id.

Three json error contracts discovered only in review round 2: (1) edit/outcome unknown-id envelopes print on STDERR not stdout; (2) the json error field strips the plain-mode "Error: " prefix; (3) record missing-flags json text = no prefix + " Example: " single space (plain has "Error: " + newline-2-space "Retry: "). Handled-error json on stderr is NOT universal — per-command probes required.
resolution: Central Failure::handled strips the prefix; per-command envelope_to_stderr set from probe evidence; pinned by differential tests.

description: Sprint 3: our format layer read records leniently (skip malformed lines, tolerate unknown types) while the reference readExpertiseFile THROWS. On a rewrite path (delete/move/delete-domain) that silently erased malformed lines and moved unknown-type records. Lesson: a lenient reader on a WRITE path is a silent-mutation hazard — the reference source is the authoritative spec for such semantics, not probes of clean stores.
resolution: Strict lib reader (records.rs) with typed MalformedLine/UnknownRecordType errors, referenced from the source; rewrites re-serialize compactly with id generation instead of copying raw lines.

name: reference-source-over-probe
description: The shipped reference package source (node_modules/@os-eco/mulch-cli/src) is the authoritative parity spec: probing clean stores missed the lenient/strict reader split, the re-serialization model (JSON.stringify, generated ids, legacy outcome normalization), config default backfill (applyConfigDefaults), domain-order semantics (JS delete vs IndexMap::swap_remove) and resolveRecordId (bare hash, unique prefix, Ambiguous). Read the source BEFORE implementing any command that mutates shared state.

name: store-policies-ownership
description: The .mulch store has ONE owner in the lib (StoreFiles): StoreLocation discovery, config mutations, and the explicit policies — read_records(domain, allow_unknown) (strict: typed MalformedLine/UnknownRecordType before any write; the flag tolerates unregistered types only), read_lines(domain) for reporting commands that must name the offending line, domain_modified(), rewrite_domain (compact canonical re-serialization + id generation + 0-byte for empty), append_domain_line (verbatim, newline guard). The CLI keeps only rendering, messages and channels (commands::open_store owns the no-store policy).

name: outcome-read-only-contract
description: outcome without --status is a READ-ONLY command in the reference (0.10.7): empty notice / colored-free listing (`Outcomes for <id> (N):` + `  i. status (agent)` + detail lines duration/tests/notes/recorded in THAT order) / json envelope with the raw outcomes array; --quiet suppresses plain only, never json; store bytes untouched, exit 0. The old CLI appended a schema-invalid outcome there. Probe-pinned 2026-10-04.

name: js-engine-byte-contracts-corrupt-stores
description: Hand-corrupted stores expose JS engine byte-contracts worth pinning: JS truthiness ([] and {} are TRUTHY — a `notes: []` line prints empty), template stringification ([1,2] joins to "1,2", null item -> empty, {} -> "[object Object]", missing field -> "undefined"), and non-array outcomes: header uses the value's .length (string char count) on stdout, then the JSC `outcomes.entries is not a function. (In 'outcomes.entries()', ...)` error on stderr with exit 1 — while json mode succeeds with the RAW value, exit 0. All probe-verified 2026-10-04, ml 0.10.7.

name: record-duplicate-contract
description: record duplicate contract (ml 0.10.7): dedupe NEVER matches ids — the registry dedupKey does (convention=content, pattern/reference/guide=name, failure=description, decision=title; unknown types never duplicate; both-sides-missing matches like undefined===undefined). Named types (all but convention/failure) UPSERT in place: fresh recorded_at, new values win, id recomputed (stale rename ids self-correct), outcomes merge existing-first, compact rewrite, `✓ Updated existing <type> in <domain> (record #N)` / json action=updated+index+record. Anonymous types skip with the advisory / json action=skipped+index (no record). Dry-run mirrors via wouldDo. Batch dedupes against the working copy (within-batch dups upsert; dry-run counts store-only so a within-batch dup is another create).

name: id-placement-contract
description: Id placement on writes (probe-pinned 2026-10-04): generated ids ONLY fill gaps (reference writeExpertiseFile `if (!r.id)`) — an explicit batch id SURVIVES upsert and create at its input key position. Flag-path upsert key order: builder fields, merged outcomes, id LAST (id is a write-time product; our builder pre-assigns and lib upsert_record lifts it). Batch upsert key order: input keys, recorded_at/classification enrichment, outcomes appended (or in-place when present), generated id LAST — input ids never move. Flag-path builder key order: outcomes BEFORE dir_anchors (record.ts:82-86).

name: one-store-one-shape
description: After bf22 the lib has exactly ONE store owner (StoreFiles: locate/discovery, config mutations, read/write policies) and ONE record shape (serde_json::Value + LineRecord). The old Store/Record pair (test-only consumer, 4 dead methods, byte-identical write_config duplicated) is gone; RecordId/CANONICAL_ORDER/REQUIRED_FIELDS died with it. Deletion-test lesson: a parallel API kept alive by its own test is debt — the roundtrip corpus now tests the module the CLI actually runs on. Roundtrip fixtures pin field order via json! literals (preserve_order keeps insertion order).

name: lenient-vs-strict-readers
description: Two reader contracts (ml 0.10.7): STRICT readExpertiseFile (mutating commands + status) skips blank AND # comment lines, normalizes legacy outcome, errors on malformed/unknown-types, crashes on scalars (ours: clean NotAnObject, DEVIATIONS). LENIENT = the raw per-line loops of validate/doctor: only blanks skip, # comments ARE Invalid-JSON findings, findings carry physical line numbers. lib: read_strict vs read_lenient (LenientLine). Never blur them — comment-skip in the lenient reader was a sprint-8 regression caught by review.

name: status-json-js-quirks
description: status json byte-contracts (probe-pinned): typeDistribution counts ANY record under String(key) — numeric types coerce to keys ("5") and JS sorts integer-like keys FIRST before insertion-order string keys; classificationDistribution increments only the three seeded keys — any other key is NaN -> JSON null; stale requires an explicit known classification (unknown -> never stale); rotting = floor(total-hours/24) of NEWEST recorded_at vs observational shelf life (NOT stale count), plain suffix ` ⚠ ROTTING (no writes in Xd)` after the governance threshold suffixes; governance_utilization = Math.round(count/max*100). jiff pitfall: span.get_hours() is the hours FIELD, use .total(Unit::Hour).

name: identifier-resolution-contract
description: Reference resolveRecordId (ml 0.10.7), used by delete/move/edit/outcome alike: strip `mx-`, exact match on mx-<hash> FIRST, then unique prefix; ambiguous -> `Error: Ambiguous identifier "<input>" matches N records: <ids>. Use more characters to disambiguate.`; not-found keeps the INPUT identifier in the text. Output surfaces print the RESOLVED record id (reference `record.id ?? id` — the fallback is dead since resolution only matches identified records). Case-sensitive, duplicate ids -> first wins. lib: resolve_record_id + ResolveError { NotFound(String), Ambiguous { identifier, count, ids } }; CLI texts live in commands::resolve_failure.

name: required-set-and-batch-order
description: Required-set contract (ml 0.10.7, sprint 10): every oneOf branch requires type + payload fields + classification + recorded_at, in THAT array order — the per-branch sub-error is the FIRST missing of that list, else `/type must be equal to constant` (never "missing type"). Sub-errors render with their ajv path: " " + message for the empty path (so validate's join produces two spaces: "…';  must have…") and "/type must be equal…" with one. Plain rendering is "  " + path + " " + message per line (missing → 3 leading spaces, const → 2); the batch entry is `Record ${i}: ${subs}` + `. Hint: …` ONLY for registered types, and non-object items read `Record ${i}:  must be object`. Batch records are normalized (recorded_at/classification when absent — explicit values survive) BEFORE validation (reference processStdinRecords).

name: batch-surfaces-contract
description: Batch surfaces contract (ml 0.10.7, sprint 11): dry-run plain = '✓ Dry-run complete. Would process {created+updated} record(s) in {d}:' + conditional '  Create/Update/Skip: n' lines + the Run-without hint; all-zero batch prints 'No records would be processed.' Normal plain = '✓ Created n record(s) in d' / '✓ Updated n record(s) in d' / 'Skipped n duplicate(s) in d', each only when non-zero, zero batch prints nothing (quiet-gated). The batch write guards on created>0 || updated>0 (record.ts:419) — skip-only/empty batches leave the file byte-identical; when it writes it goes through writeExpertiseFile (compact: comments/blanks drop, id-less survivors get ids, missing trailing newline repaired, 0-byte store fine). Named store-dups count as Update in dry-run AND normal; anon dups skip; within-batch dups upsert in normal (working copy) but count as creates in dry-run (store-only dedupe). The FLAG path keeps its verbatim append.

name: unknown-domain-surfaces
description: Unknown-domain surfaces (ml 0.10.7): FIVE per-command variants exist — standard plain (two-line lowercase 'Error: domain ...\nAvailable domains: ...'), json one-liner (capital D, no Error prefix — IDENTICAL for every command incl. move), move's plain (capital D single line = 'Error: ' + the json sentence), delete-domain's plain (Hint line instead of the list), and (future) query/rank/prime/search (capital-D + Hint with `ml add` wording) + ready ('Available:' wording). One adapter commands::unknown_domain_failure(command, domain, available, json, DomainFailure::{Standard,Move,WithHint}) owns the join + shapes; json text is shape-independent (orthogonal to plain). Pin per-command when new commands land — the reference wording is inconsistent on purpose.

name: record-type-registry
description: Record-type registry (sprint 13): lib ids.rs REGISTRY = six TypeSpec rows {name, payload fields, id_key, named} in the reference's fixed order. Everything else derives or is test-pinned: id_key_field/is_named_type/payload_fields are lookups (fallbacks: unknown -> content key, named, content-only payload), schema branches() = type + payload + classification + recorded_at per row, status TYPES = PAYLOAD_TYPES (pinned == REGISTRY names), record/edit flag tables pin the payload-name universe. A registry row gaining a field without plumbing now fails a unit test, not a silent drift. b8ca's per-field subschemas extend THIS table.

name: schema-validation-model
description: Schema validation model (sprint 14, ml 0.10.7): each branch reports its FIRST failing PROPERTY in order required -> additionalProperties -> properties in reference declaration order (baseSchemaProps keys: id, classification, recorded_at, evidence, tags, relates_to, supersedes, outcomes, dir_anchors, supersession_demoted_at, anchor_decay_demoted_at, owner, status; then the type const; then payload fields; then the branch optional fields). A property with several failing keywords reports ALL (type:true -> "/type must be string" + "/type must be equal to constant"; non-string classification/status -> type + enum). required checks KEY PRESENCE (null is present and fails the type check). Branch optional lists: pattern/reference declare files, decision declares date — elsewhere those keys are additionalProperties. The record FLAG path emits only required ∪ optional fields (--files on guide is dropped). All surfaces (validate plain/json, doctor, batch entries, move) share one evaluator incl. the oneOf tail.

name: doctor-duplicates-contract
description: Doctor duplicates contract (ml 0.10.7, sprint 15): checkDuplicates iterates config-domain order, per PARSED record i (skip first), findDuplicate over the prefix returns the FIRST same-type record with ===-equal dedupKey value; count = redundant records (one detail each: "<domain>: duplicate <type> at index <i+1> (matches #<j+1>)", 1-based parsed indexes, NOT line numbers); warn, fixable false, --fix never touches them; unknown types parse but never duplicate (no registry def). findDuplicate ===-semantics: numbers as f64 (1 === 1.0), objects/arrays NEVER match (identity), undefined only equals undefined (both missing), null only null. Clean store: pass "No duplicates" byte-identical. Extension (ours, README DEVIATIONS): repeated id with structurally divergent content = fail-class "<N> divergent id(s) found" details "<domain>: divergent id <id> at index N (matches #M, different content)", never auto-fixed; mixed store combines messages with "; ". Rust seam: lib find_duplicate + js_dedup_eq (records.rs) — the never-match arm MUST precede the structural-eq arm (a reorder silently matches identical object shapes; pinned by unit test).

name: outcome-entry-duration-contract
description: Outcome-entry + duration contract (ml 0.10.7, sprint 16, C1 seam): ONE lib owner OutcomeEntry::build (records.rs) — key order per family is DIFFERENT and probe-pinned: record/edit write status,duration,test_results,agent (no recorded_at, no notes); outcome writes status,recorded_at,duration,agent,notes,test_results. Duration parse = reference numeric-flags.ts: regex shape digits/[.digits] ONLY (rejects -5, 1e3, .5, 5., 1.2.3, spaces, unicode), then EVERYTHING through f64 so JS Number rounding applies above 2^53 (9007199254740993 stores 9007199254740992; integral values keep full-digit integer form through i64::MAX -> byte-identical; above i64::MAX serde float form vs stringify decimal expansion = documented README deviation). Error bytes: `--<flag> must be a non-negative number (got "x").` — plain = `Error: ` prefix on stderr via Failure::handled_on_stderr (message carries the prefix, handled() strips it for the json envelope, envelope on STDERR), exit 1, NOTHING written. CLI: duration flags need allow_hyphen_values=true or clap eats `-5` as an unknown flag before the parse ever runs (commander passes it through). Edit family builds the outcome ONLY with --outcome-status present (duration without status is ignored silently, both sides).

name: mixed-batch-nested-contract
description: Mixed-batch + nested-subschema contract (ml 0.10.7, sprint 17): (1) PARTIAL WRITES — processStdinRecords validates per record (normalize recorded_at/classification FIRST), collects `Record i: <ajv errors>` entries for failures, writes the valid ones against a MUTATING working copy (within-batch dups upsert; dry-run counts against the unmutated existing only), single rewrite under guard created>0||updated>0; caller prints the error block BEFORE the surfaces (plain: `Validation errors:` + `  entry` lines on stderr; json: error envelope {success:false,command,error:"Validation errors: joined"} on STDERR + result envelope on stdout), result success = errors-empty || created+updated>0, exit 1 ONLY when errors>0 && created+updated===0 (dry-run same formula; the old 2026-10-04 probe note rc=1-for-partial was stale — source wins). (2) NESTED subschemas (plain `new Ajv()`, allErrors effectively fail-fast per keyword group): outcome item = status required + enum(success/failure/partial) + duration number + test_results/agent/notes/recorded_at strings + additionalProperties false; FIRST failing item only; within item required -> additional -> first failing property WITH ALL ITS keywords (bad-string status: enum only; non-string: type+enum); evidence = additionalProperties then string fields in def order (commit,date,issue,file,bead,seeds,gh,linear); base property evaluation order = baseSchemaProps declaration order (evidence < tags < relates_to < supersedes < outcomes < dir_anchors) — schema.rs BASE_PROPERTIES + nested fns model this. (3) C2 seam: lib upsert_plan (Create | Update{index,merged=merge_outcomes(existing-first)} | Skip{index}; force->Create) — flag path post-step = id LIFTED LAST (builder pre-assigns), batch post-step = entry().or_insert (input-id position, generated after outcomes); upsert_record deleted. Rust seam: UpsertPlan in records.rs.

name: staleness-verdict-contract
description: Staleness contract (ml 0.10.7, sprint 18, C5 seam): TWO IDENTICAL reference fns — isStale (prune.ts:51, doctor check+fix) and isRecordStale (utils/expertise.ts:305, audit/calculateDomainHealth=status) — one rule: foundational -> never; MISSING/UNKNOWN/NON-STRING classification -> never (fall-through false, NOT a tactical default); recorded_at unparsable/missing -> NaN age -> never; boundary = Math.floor(age_days) > shelf, i.e. stale from the FIRST instant of the (shelf+1)-th day (14.9d fresh, 15.0d stale under shelf 14; NOT age>=shelf which is up to 24h early). Port seam: StaleRule::verdict(&Value, now) -> Fresh | Stale | Unparsable (stale.rs) — the ONE extraction owner for status stale count, doctor check, doctor --fix. doctor --fix REPORT ORDER = check order (applyFixes cases: schema-validation Removed lines for ALL domains first, then stale-records Pruned lines), not per-domain interleave. FIXTURE RULE for time-dependent parity tests: derive recorded_at from the runtime clock (jiff dev-dep in cli_parity), never fixed calendar dates — fresh-side fixtures are time bombs crossing the (shelf+1)-day boundary (spec-review catch: fixed 2026-09-22 fixture would flip the battery 15h after landing; fresh cases sit a full day inside their shelf, stale a full day past).

name: doctor-repair-case-order
description: The doctor --fix contract (verified against ml 0.10.7 applyFixes, sprint 19): repairs iterate the CHECKS array in check order — jsonl-integrity, legacy-outcome, schema-validation, stale-records — each gated on status!=pass AND fixable, each RE-READING the file the previous pass rewrote; report lines follow that check order (Migrated sits between the two Removed classes, stale+invalid counts as Removed because schema runs first). Repairs run BEFORE any rendering in both modes — a crashing reference repair prints no report at all — and the JSON envelope carries a fixed array whenever --fix ran (empty allowed). Write models per pass: jsonl and legacy preserve raw lines verbatim (survivors trimmed, migrated lines compact with outcomes appended at end); schema and stale re-serialize canonically (write_records semantics incl. id backfill). The schema keep rule is !registry.get(type) || validate — unknown-type AND typeless records stay, flagged only (mulch-d45c data loss). Reference crash classes we deviate from (README): malformed lines crash its checks before any report; id-less unknown-type records crash its rewrites (generateRecordId); we report/repair.

name: config-defaults-contract
description: Config default contract (verified vs ml 0.10.7 utils/config.ts applyConfigDefaults + schemas/config.ts DEFAULT_CONFIG, sprint 21): governance 100/150/200 and shelf-life 14/30 are the FORMAT CONTRACT, owned by Governance::reference_default()/ShelfLife::reference_default() in config.rs; every consumer goes through Config::effective_governance()/effective_shelf_life(), which read the per-field-backfilled mappings — partial blocks KEEP their set values (governance {max_entries: 5} -> 5/150/200; shelf {tactical: 1} -> 1/30), matching the reference's shallow spread. The old typed readers (governance()/shelf_life()) dropped partial blocks WHOLESALE (no serde defaults -> Err -> None -> full-default fallback) — that was the bug 53cb fixed; keep them as the strict erroring surface for callers that want errors. Wrong-typed fields fall back wholesale (documented + pinned). StaleRule::from_shelf_life takes the effective value; verdict compares in plain i64 milliseconds ((days+1).saturating_mul(86_400_000) vs now-recorded ms) — exact ms parity with Math.floor(age)>shelf AND overflow-proof: jiff Span::hours panics above 175,307,616 hours, so the old span-arithmetic shape could panic in debug / invert the verdict for saturated shelves.

name: legacy-outcome-value-law
description: Legacy singular `outcome` law (ml 0.10.7, sprint 22, mulch-15d3/1609): DETECTION = singular `outcome` key without `outcomes`, on objects, value NEVER inspected (null detects — lib records::legacy_outcome). EXTRACTION = present-keys-only status/duration/test_results/agent in that order (legacy_entry); NON-OBJECT values yield the EMPTY entry — the reference spreads undefined fields which JSON drops: observable contract = listing `  1. undefined`, json `[{}]`, append writes `[{}, new]` (mulch-1609's literal `[5]` shorthand was imprecise; observables are the contract). NULL outcome NEVER migrates (raw.outcome !== null guard): key survives rewrites untouched, edit/move still ABORT on it. Mid-object rewrites: remaining keys keep order, `outcomes` appended at line END — serde preserve_order `Map::remove` SWAPS the last key into the hole (latent id-promotion bug, fixed with shift_remove in normalize + migrate). edit/move verdicts run over the reference's IN-MEMORY shape: raw key presence decides (re-add via read_lenient physical line), strict-reader normalization must not leak into the gate.

name: governance-check-contract
description: Doctor governance check (ml 0.10.7, sprint 23, mulch-dd36): per domain IN CONFIG ORDER, count = leniently parsed records (malformed lines don't count — the reference crashes there, our jsonl-integrity deviation); tiers: count>=hard_limit -> FAIL detail '{domain}: {n} records (over hard limit of {h})' (doctor exits 1); count>=warn_entries -> warn '(over warn threshold of {w})'; count>=max_entries -> warn '(approaching limit of {m})'; worst-status-wins; any details -> message '{n} domain(s) over governance thresholds', fixable ALWAYS false (--fix never touches counts, store bytes unchanged, no Fixed block); none -> pass 'All domains within governance limits'. Thresholds come from Config::effective_governance() (partial blocks backfill per field). Implementation note: bind the (status, threshold, wording) triple to the BRANCH, never re-derive wording by value equality — warn_entries==hard_limit degenerate configs would mis-word otherwise.

name: twin-store-fs-order-determinism
description: Differential parity against readdir-order surfaces: the reference CLI iterates directories unsorted (Node/Bun readdir), and Rust read_dir walks the SAME unsorted stream - twin stores (identical file sets) list identically, so raw iteration order is the parity-exact choice and a sort would BE the deviation. Applies wherever the reference lists store files (doctor orphaned-domains adoption order; verified by the sprint-24 multi-orphan battery pin).

content: Differential battery fixtures with schema-valid records must carry the FULL oneOf required set: type + the branch's payload fields + classification + recorded_at. Use classification foundational + fixed recorded_at 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z: never stale (foundational never decays), constant bytes across twin stores (no sub-second flake in file comparisons). Missing classification/recorded_at makes every fixture record schema-invalid; the schema repair deletes them on --fix and anchor/orphan assertions silently pin the wrong empty store (sprint 24).

name: ml-record-type-specific-required-flags
description: ml record's --type gates additional required flags: failure requires --resolution, convention requires --content (retry message names the missing flag). Pass them on the first call: failure = description (what happened) + resolution (the rule/fix), convention = description (one-liner) + content (the actual rule text). Observed as two CLI retries in sprint 24.

name: ml-reference-has-per-file-oexcl-writer-lock
description: ml 0.10.7 src/utils/lock.ts: withFileLock(filePath, fn) locks EACH store file with an O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile at "<filePath>.lock" — 50ms retry, 5s timeout (error: "Timed out waiting for lock on <path>. If no other mulch process is running, delete the lock file manually."), 30s mtime-staleness recovery (unlink + retry), unlink on release. Callers: record/edit/outcome/delete/delete-domain/move (move NESTS target+source locks — ordering hazard)/doctor/prune/archive/compact/setup/onboard; the lock wraps the whole read->mutate->write cycle; dry-run branches read lock-free; hooks fire outside. Weaknesses (why mulch deviates to flock, mulch-228d): a crashed holder leaves the lockfile wedging writers <=30s or until manual deletion; staleness-steal can double-admit a >30s holder; config writes (domain auto-create) race outside the per-file lock. mulch port: kernel-owned flock on ONE permanent .mulch/.lock, README DEVIATIONS bullet.

name: ml-custom-types-full-law
description: ml 0.10.7 custom_types law (probed 2026-10-15, mulch-b4bd): isNamedType = builtin not-in-{convention,failure}, CUSTOM dedup_key!=content_hash; id = sha6("type:" + String(record[idKey] ?? "")) with idKey = id_key ?? dedup_key ?? parent.idKey ?? dedupKey (content_hash reads an ABSENT field -> all such records share one id); findDuplicate: content_hash -> null, field === semantics (undefined===undefined matches); the oneOf iterates builtins then customs in config order; doctor type_registry computes "N type(s) registered: B built-in, C custom" with "{name} (built-in|custom): {n} record(s)" details; move/delete summaries render the COMPILED summary template; the global config-error surface (cli.ts registry-init handler): plain 2-line stderr rc1, json envelope on stderr with command:"init" HARDCODED for every command; registry/custom.ts validation quirk: a STRING required/optional iterates its CHARACTERS, custom_types-as-string yields (index,char) entries, TOKEN_RE is case-insensitive (gi) so {Name} extracts then fails the declared-fields check.

name: custom-types-flag-path-law
description: ml 0.10.7 record/edit flag path is custom-type aware (probed 2026-10-16): --type choices = registry.names() (builtins + customs) enforced by commander AT PARSE TIME; custom fields register dynamic --<hyphenated> flags (value_name keeps underscores; fields overlapping declared flags read the existing flag - declaredOptionNames skip); collectField iterates required then optional (empty = missing-required / dropped-optional); the missing-flags hint hyphenates the flag but the placeholder keeps underscores; customs have NO positional fallback (positionalFallbackField is builtin-only); extracts_files fields comma-split AND auto-populate from getContextFiles (staged+unstaged git diff --name-only, deduped, sorted) when absent - builtins pattern/reference ride the same law; edit def loop = raw flag view (empty strings store, --files empty stores []) over required+optional, unregistered types write NO payload fields; buildRetryCommand echoes builtin flags only - provided custom flags never appear, missing ones append last.

name: custom-types-aliases-law
description: The reference's aliases: config block validated by validateCustomTypeConfig (9 rules, byte-exact wording incl. the JSON.stringify-rendered invalid-name family; canonical keys must be declared; legacy names collide with base fields, foreign BUILTIN fields (unless declared here), current fields, double use). Read-time applyAliases (utils/expertise.ts): canonical wins unless missing/null/empty-string; legacy keys delete order-preservingly; new canonical keys APPEND at object end in config order. Seam map: readExpertiseFile (our read_strict + StoreFiles::read_lenient) applies aliases; validate.ts + doctor checkSchemaValidation apply before Ajv on their own parses; doctor's FIX passes read via readExpertiseFile (canonical rewrites) EXCEPT legacy-outcome + jsonl-integrity (raw). CRITICAL CORNER: doctor's checkLegacyOutcome reads RAW bytes — outcome (singular) is a legal alias legacy name, so the check must NOT see the canonicalized record (spec-review find 2026-10-17).

name: reference-probe-config-quoted-version
description: Probe configs for the reference ml CLI need the version scalar QUOTED: `version: '1'` (or "1") at .mulch/mulch.config.yaml — an unquoted 1 parses as an integer and the config surface diverges before any parity probe can run. Domain/expertise files live at .mulch/expertise/. Came out of HANDOFF's 'Known ephemera' (file removed 2026-10-17 — ephemera now live here, not in a handoff file).

name: custom-types-render-hooks-law
description:
Reference custom-type render hooks (ml 0.10.7 registry/custom.ts), probed byte-exactly 2026-10-18 (/tmp/sprint34/c1-probes, 7 stores + 28 raw outputs). Consumers: our render.rs generic hooks (mulch-bb38).

MARKDOWN (per type, `### <sectionTitle>`): `- <idTag>**<summary>** — f: v; f: v (<files>)<meta>` — summary NOT truncated and its source fields REPEAT in the detail; detail = declared fields payload-then-optional, null AND "" skip, files never in detail; files parens AFTER the detail; meta = links (query) or class/evidence/tags+links (prime --full).
COMPACT: `- [<type_name>] <truncate(summary,100)> (<files>) (<id>, <class>[, <Xm|h|d> ago][, ★N])[ <outcome>][ <links>]` — raw type name, sentence-boundary truncate (first [.!?]\s in (0,100) keeps punctuation, else cut 100+"..."), TWO paren groups when files exist, `foundational` has NO age suffix, ★ only when score>0 (integer or one decimal), outcome bracket = LAST entry's symbol/duration/@agent + TOTAL count (Nx).
XML: one `<f>v</f>` per DECLARED field (payload-then-optional), arrays joined ", ", files included; only null/absent skip — "" -> `<f></f>` and [] -> `<files></files>` (markdown skips both).
PLAIN: customs are INVISIBLE by design (plainSection's switch default returns []) but still count in the header.
SECTION TITLE chain: `cfg.section_title ?? parent.sectionTitle ?? Capitalize(name)+"s"` — JS ?? so non-strings render as their display string (`123` -> `### 123`, `""` -> `### `); naive +s (`status` -> `Statuss`); extends-without-title inherits the parent builtin's title (`### Patterns`); markdown ONLY.
ORDER: markdown/plain group by registry.enabled() = 6 builtins canonical then customs in CONFIG insertion order (never alphabetical); compact/xml stay in DISK record order; empty sections drop entirely; unregistered types skip silently.

Our port status: mulch-bb38 landed all of it (Row.section_title + the RenderRow enum); unit pins in render.rs build the four-custom fixture.

name: corpus-query-laws
description: AMENDMENT (sprint 34 review, evidence 2fa23e4): the EMPTY prime union means EVERY domain in config insertion order — prime.ts:243 `targetDomains = unique.length > 0 ? unique : Object.keys(config.domains)` — so bare prime primes everything; exclusions still filter the all-set afterwards (empty union + exclusion = all minus excluded). First implementation returned [] contradicting its own doc line; the spec reviewer caught it against the reference source. Law now pinned in query.rs tests (domain_set_union_dedups_and_excludes).
